correctness.rationale: The equality of the two ordered side-size truncations is necessary because every graph in the family has clique number equal to its larger side and independence number equal to its smaller side. For sufficiency, in any q moves a coordinate equality pattern can be replicated between two finite sets whose cardinalities agree below q or are both at least q; the independent replication on the two coordinates preserves all vertex equality and adjacency atoms. The EF theorem yields the universal equivalence. The class indicators use only thresholds of rank <=q; exact class count, sharp q² bound and least distinguishing rank follow. Standalone finite extension-type enumeration was actually executed and its output checked; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim completely classifies every quantifier-depth theory in a natural infinite two-parameter graph family, proves sharp parameter and vertex cutoffs, and determines the exact optimal distinguishing rank for every pair. In a graph-only signature that forgets row/column labels, it establishes the stronger rank-preserving semantic collapse of every bounded-rank sentence to a Boolean combination of two existential cardinality thresholds. This is a structural logical normal form with genuine family-wide content, not one more isolated finite count.
